note: Not yet modelled: the individual income tax instrument needs an income tax schedule, a calibrated income tax base, which this country-year lacks. See the other notes for why. Income tax schedules come from the OECD Tax Database, which covers OECD members only; other countries need hand-curated schedules.

Groups are the 127 g-percentiles of Gethin & Fisher-Post (2026), "Government Redistribution and Global Poverty Reduction", data version 2026-09-22: all individuals, with income split equally within couples (WID's 999j unit), ranked by pretax national income. Sizes and average incomes are theirs.

Amounts are in national currency at 2023 prices: Gethin-Fisher values (PPP USD of 2024) times defl (0.969947) times xppp_us (0.716798). Their ReadMe gives the PPP base year as 2023, but xppp_us matches WID's 2024 PPP, so we take the base to be 2024.
Check: total pretax income from Gethin-Fisher is 0.983 times WID's national income for 2023.

Lower thresholds come from WID's tptinc999j for 2023, made nominal and scaled by each group's ratio of Gethin-Fisher's to WID's average income (122 of 126 groups; 4 unscaled where that ratio was unavailable or outside 0.5-2). The bottom group's threshold is set to 0, since Gethin-Fisher's averages don't follow WID's negative incomes.
1 thresholds fell outside the averages of the groups on either side and were moved to the nearer one: p60p61.

The current income tax rate by group (effectiveIncomeTaxShareOfIncome) is Gethin-Fisher's personal income tax (tax_dir_pit, their central estimate) over pretax income. Their lower and upper bounds aren't used.
5 groups have non-positive average income; their rate is set to 0.
Data quality Modeled, from WID's data-quality score of 3 (out of 5) on the income thresholds: 4 or 5 is Credible, lower is Modeled.
No calibrated income tax base: there is no income tax schedule for this country-year.

No 2023 income tax schedule from the OECD Tax Database, "Personal income tax (PIT) - central government rates and thresholds" (SDMX dataflow OECD.CTP.TPS,DSD_TAX_PIT@DF_PIT_CENT). Germany's income tax tariff is a formula: in two zones the marginal rate rises continuously, so the OECD table gives thresholds but no rates for them. No schedule is generated; it needs to be approximated by many small brackets computed from the statutory formula (§32a EStG), or transcribed by hand.

Solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag), for when Germany is included: it is a surcharge on income tax, not on income. On salary income it applies only above an exemption threshold, then rises gradually through a transition zone toward its full rate of 5.5% of income tax, so it is effectively progressive; on capital income (taxed under the flat withholding tax) it is a flat 5.5% of the tax. Computing it exactly would be fairly complicated. A reasonable simplification is to inflate total income tax by 3-4%, as the average solidarity surcharge net of exemptions. Reference: https://bruttonettorechnen.de/en/guides/solidarity-surcharge-guide/

Germany's schedule can't yet be used even if transcribed: in two zones its marginal rate rises continuously, and the model does not yet have a way to apply a partly continuous schedule to its excess curves.
